arguments.summary: Latest SEC normalized facts establish high reported profitability and operating cash generation for ANET, MU, META and NVDA, but do not provide comparable prior-period facts, detailed filing risk language, earnings guidance, or market-derived valuation multiples. Thus only explicitly assumed EPS×P/E sensitivities—not investable valuation conclusions—are supported. QQQ is not treated as an issuer; its dated look-through separately shows NVDA, MU and META weights.

claims.text: ANET's latest reported 10-Q covers the six months ended 2026-06-30: revenue was $5.7447bn, net income $2.2358bn, operating cash flow $2.7765bn, capex $84.2m, and diluted EPS $1.75; reported operating and net margins were 44.14% and 38.92%.

An illustrative ANET base sensitivity annualizes the reported six-month EPS to $3.50 and applies an assumed 50x P/E, yielding $175/share. This is neither consensus nor a forecast and extends beyond the reported period.

MU's latest reported 10-Q covers 2025-08-29 through 2026-05-28: revenue was $78.959bn, net income $47.268bn, operating cash flow $45.702bn, capex $19.602bn, and diluted EPS $41.40; reported operating and net margins were 70.40% and 59.86%.

META's latest reported 10-Q covers the six months ended 2026-06-30: revenue was $117.111bn, net income $42.621bn, operating cash flow $64.088bn, capex $49.113bn, and diluted EPS $16.62. Long-term debt was reported at $83.664bn; operating and net margins were 35.56% and 36.39%.

NVDA's latest reported 10-Q covers 2026-01-26 through 2026-07-26: revenue was $177.837bn, net income $118.010bn, operating cash flow $74.421bn, and diluted EPS $4.85; reported operating and net margins were 65.94% and 66.36%.

The sponsor-supplied QQQ holdings table dated 2026-09-12 lists NVDA at 8.45%, MU at 4.85%, and META at 3.07%; its status is stale under the supplied seven-day maximum-age rule. ANET is not shown in the supplied holdings list.

The reported financial data support a 21/63-session catalyst framework centered on subsequent earnings releases and demand/capacity disclosures, but do not themselves establish sequential or year-over-year growth, competitive positioning, or a valuation rerating.

gaps.description: Prior-period comparatives, detailed 10-Q/earnings-release demand, customer concentration, competitive, capacity and guidance disclosures were not read for these issuers; SEC normalized facts alone cannot substantiate revenue/earnings/cash-flow trends or company-specific catalysts and risks.

No market-derived P/E, forward EPS, or company guidance inputs are available. Bear/base/bull EPS×P/E valuations for MU, META and NVDA—and a full three-case set for ANET—would be assumption-driven, not evidence-backed.
QQQ holdings are dated 2026-09-12 but flagged stale; look-through weights are dated fund composition rather than current exposure.

assumptions: Any annualization of an interim EPS is a scenario assumption, not a forecast.
Any P/E multiple is an explicit unverified scenario input because no market-derived multiple was supplied.
Reported interim periods differ across issuers and are not directly comparable.
arguments.counter_thesis: High interim profitability and cash generation may prove non-repeatable if subsequent demand, pricing, capacity, investment, competitive or policy disclosures deteriorate; absent verified forecasts and valuation multiples, strong reported results cannot establish upside over 21/63 sessions.

assumptions: Interim EPS annualization and P/E are illustrative only.
